cards.name: Character Styles
cards.summary: Opens (or brings forward) the Character Styles panel: the document's saved character-level formats (font, size, leading, tracking, colour, OpenType options). Clicking a style applies it to the selected text or text objects; the panel menu creates, redefines, duplicates, loads and deletes styles, and a + after a name marks local overrides.
cards.how: Select text, click a style name to apply it; Alt-click (or panel menu > Clear Overrides) to drop local formatting. New Character Style from the panel menu captures the formatting of the current selection.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Character Styles") (opens the panel; id paired by menu label, not confirmed by execution). Object-model route (unverified): var s = app.activeDocument.characterStyles.add("Caption"); s.characterAttributes.size = 9; s.applyTo(textRange, true);
use_for: same caption / subhead formatting across a multi-artboard brochure
brand type spec applied to many text frames at once
global restyle of every price or label by editing one style
avoid: one-off formatting of a single headline: set it in the Character panel instead
styles with local overrides keep the overrides; a script applying a style should pass clearingOverrides = true

cards.name: Glyphs
cards.summary: Opens the Glyphs panel from the Window > Type menu (the same panel as Type > Glyphs, which uses the id 'alternate glyph palette plugin'): a grid of every glyph in the chosen font, including alternates, ligatures, ornaments, arrows and currency symbols. Double-clicking a glyph inserts it at the text cursor or replaces the selected character.
cards.how: Pick the font and a Show filter (Entire Font, Alternates for Current Selection, Ornaments ...); with a character selected, the small triangle on a cell lists its alternates; double-click to insert.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("alternate glyph palette plugin 2") (opens the panel; id paired by the keyboard-shortcuts dialog, not confirmed by execution). To insert a character by script, write it into the text directly (unverified): textFrame.contents += "\u20B9";
use_for: inserting dingbats, arrows, stars or bullets into a poster or menu
picking swash or stylistic alternates for a logo wordmark
finding the rupee, euro or other currency sign a font actually contains
avoid: scripts cannot drive the panel; insert the Unicode character instead
alternates without a Unicode value cannot be typed by script; switch them on with OpenType features (OpenType panel) instead

cards.name: OpenType
cards.id: internal palettes posing as plug-in menus-opentype
cards.summary: Opens the OpenType panel, which switches OpenType font features on the selected text: standard and discretionary ligatures, contextual alternates, swash, stylistic and titling alternates, ordinals, fractions, figure style (tabular / proportional, lining / oldstyle), position (superscript, subscript, numerator, denominator) and stylistic sets. A button only changes the text when the font contains that feature.
cards.how: Select type, then toggle the feature buttons along the bottom of the panel; Figure and Position menus set number style; the panel menu holds Stylistic Sets.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("internal palettes posing as plug-in menus-opentype") (opens the panel; id paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). Object-model route (unverified): textRange.characterAttributes.ligature / discretionaryLigature / contextualLigature / fractions / ordinals / swash / titling / stylisticAlternates / figureStyle = FigureStyleType.TABULAR
use_for: real fractions and ordinals in a recipe card or price list
tabular lining figures so numbers line up in a table or menu
swash and discretionary ligatures on a display headline or wordmark
avoid: fonts without the feature: the button does nothing; check the font's alternates in the Glyphs panel first
outlined text can no longer be changed; set features before Create Outlines

cards.name: Paragraph
cards.id: internal palettes posing as plug-in menus-paragraph
cards.summary: Opens the Paragraph panel for paragraph-level formatting of the selected text: alignment and justification (including justify-last-line options), left / right / first-line indents, space before and after, and hyphenation; the panel menu adds the composer choice, justification and hyphenation settings and Roman hanging punctuation.
cards.how: Select the text or the text object; click an alignment button, type indent and spacing values; tick Hyphenate for justified body copy.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("internal palettes posing as plug-in menus-paragraph") (opens the panel; id paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). Object-model route (unverified): textRange.paragraphAttributes.justification = Justification.CENTER; .firstLineIndent, .spaceBefore, .spaceAfter, .hyphenation
use_for: centred headline block on a poster
justified body copy in a flyer or brochure column
hanging indents for list-style copy
avoid: many frames of body text: define a Paragraph Style instead of formatting each frame
point type has no frame width, so justification and hyphenation have nothing to work against; use area type for body copy

review.changes: avoid: replaced the vague claim that point type ignores most indents with the accurate point (no frame width for justification / hyphenation)

cards.name: Paragraph Styles
cards.summary: Opens the Paragraph Styles panel: saved formats that combine character attributes with paragraph settings (alignment, indents, spacing, hyphenation, tabs) and apply to whole paragraphs. Clicking a style applies it to the paragraphs in the selection; editing a style updates every paragraph that uses it.
cards.how: Select paragraphs and click a style; Alt-click to clear overrides; Style Options (double-click) edits the definition; New Paragraph Style captures the current formatting.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Paragraph Styles Palette") (opens the panel; id paired by label + parent menu, not confirmed by execution). Object-model route (unverified): var p = app.activeDocument.paragraphStyles.add("Body"); p.paragraphAttributes.spaceAfter = 6; p.applyTo(textRange, true);
use_for: consistent heading / body / caption hierarchy in a multi-page brochure or menu
restyling all body copy at once by editing one style
templates handed to a script that only applies named styles
avoid: single short headline: format it directly
local overrides survive applying a style unless cleared

cards.name: Reflow Viewer
cards.summary: Opens the Reflow Viewer panel, which compares the old and the updated layout of East Asian (Japanese, Chinese, Korean) text from documents made in older Illustrator versions: it marks the text objects whose layout changed, shows the old layout, the new one, or both overlaid in contrasting colours, and highlights changed line breaks, character spacing and line heights. Panel details come from Adobe's help page, not from this harvest.
cards.script_api: none: the harvest found no executeMenuCommand id for this item; it can only be reached through the menu path Window/Type/Reflow Viewer (Win32 command 2147484083) by UI automation.
use_for: checking that a legacy Japanese / Chinese / Korean packaging or poster file kept its line breaks after its text was updated
proofing East Asian copy for reflow before an old file goes to print
avoid: Latin-only documents: there is no legacy East Asian layout to compare
editing or formatting text: use the Character and Paragraph panels
cards.how: Open the legacy document, open the panel, turn on marking of affected text, then switch between the old, new and overlay views and check the highlighted line-break, spacing and line-height changes; fix text that reflowed badly before export.

review.changes: summary/how/use_for/avoid rewritten: Reflow Viewer compares old vs updated East Asian text layouts in legacy documents (Adobe help), it is not a large-size text reader; dropped the CDR Text/Edit Text equivalent (different job); script_api no longer suggests textFrame.contents

cards.name: Tabs
cards.id: internal palettes posing as plug-in menus-tab
cards.summary: Opens the Tabs panel, a ruler that snaps above the selected text frame for setting tab stops: left, centre, right and decimal-aligned tabs, their positions, and a leader string (e.g. dots) that fills the gap. Text separated by tab characters lines up on these stops.
cards.how: Select the text frame, click a tab-type button, click on the ruler to place a stop (or type X), add a Leader such as '. '; the magnet icon re-aligns the ruler to the frame.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("internal palettes posing as plug-in menus-tab") (opens the panel; id paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). Object-model route (unverified): build TabStopInfo objects (alignment, position, leader) and assign textRange.paragraphAttributes.tabStops = [ ... ];
use_for: restaurant menu with dish names and dot-leader prices
price lists and spec sheets with aligned columns
decimal-aligned figures in a simple table
avoid: text without tab characters: stops change nothing
complex tables with wrapping cells: build separate text frames on a grid instead

cards.name: Variables
cards.summary: Opens the Variables panel for data-driven graphics: bind text, linked-file, visibility and graph-data variables to objects, capture data sets (one row of values each), switch between them, and load or save variable libraries as XML, so one template produces many versions.
cards.how: Select an object, choose Make Text Dynamic / Make Visibility Dynamic / Make Linked File Dynamic from the panel; change the content and Capture Data Set for each version; Load / Save Variable Library for XML exchange.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Variables Palette Menu Item") (opens the panel; id paired by label + parent menu, not confirmed by execution). Object-model route (unverified): var v = doc.variables.add(); v.kind = VariableKind.TEXTUAL; textFrame.contentVariable = v; doc.dataSets.add(); doc.importVariables(File(xmlPath));
use_for: name badges, certificates or ID cards from a list
localised or per-city versions of one banner
templated social cards with swapped headline and photo
avoid: data comes as XML only; for a long CSV a script looping over rows and setting textFrame.contents is often simpler
graph-data variables only bind to Illustrator graph objects

cards.name: Version History
cards.summary: Opens the Version History panel for a cloud document (.aic): it lists saved versions with timestamps and lets you preview, restore, save a version as a copy, or mark a version so it is kept beyond the retention period. A local .ai file has no versions to show.
cards.script_api: none: the harvest found no executeMenuCommand id; reach it only through the menu path Window/Version History (Win32 command 2147484380) by UI automation.
use_for: rolling a client logo back to an earlier round
marking approved milestones of a cloud design file
avoid: local .ai files: save numbered copies (logo_v01.ai, logo_v02.ai) instead

cards.name: Manage Workspaces...
cards.summary: Opens the Manage Workspaces dialog listing your saved workspaces, where you can rename or delete them or create a new one from the current panel layout. The menu walk found the item disabled with no document open.
cards.how: Select a workspace in the list and type over its name to rename it, use the New Workspace icon to save a copy of the current layout, or the trash icon to delete it; OK commits.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Manage Workspace") would only open the dialog. The harvest's two id matchers disagree (dialog alignment suggested 'Adobe Reset Workspace'), so the id is not confirmed. There is no object-model access to workspaces.
use_for: cleaning up old workspaces
renaming a production workspace before sharing a setup
avoid: switching workspaces: pick one under Window > Workspace or the workspace switcher instead

review.changes: summary: 'duplicate' -> create from the current layout; removed PS Window/Workspace/Delete Workspace (only deletes, not the same job)

cards.name: New Workspace...
cards.summary: Saves the current arrangement of panels, toolbars and docks as a named workspace that then appears under Window > Workspace and in the workspace switcher. The menu walk found it disabled with no document open.
cards.how: Type a name and click OK; using an existing workspace name overwrites that workspace.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe New Workspace") (opens the naming dialog; id paired by label, not confirmed by execution). There is no object-model access to workspaces.
use_for: saving a typography or packaging layout of panels for repeat jobs
a clean layout for screen recording or teaching
avoid: expecting it to store tool settings or preferences: it stores panel layout only

cards.name: Reset
cards.summary: Resets the current workspace to its saved panel layout, putting back panels that were moved, closed or opened since (the menu walk read the label as Reset; the Keyboard Shortcuts dialog lists it as Reset "Current Workspace"). The document is not touched. The menu walk found it disabled with no document open.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Reset Workspace") (id paired by label + parent menu; the dialog alignment suggested 'arrangeicon' instead, so not confirmed by execution).
use_for: recovering a lost or scattered panel layout
starting an automated or recorded session from a known layout
avoid: keeping a changed layout: save it with New Workspace... first, Reset discards it

review.changes: summary: the live label was walked as 'Reset', not Reset "<workspace name>"; now cites the kbsc name Reset "Current Workspace" from the batch

cards.name: Activate...
cards.summary: Leftover id from the serial-number licensing era (Help > Activate... in Illustrator CS3 to CS6, which opened the product-activation dialog). Creative Cloud versions license through Adobe ID sign-in; 30.2.1 has no menu item for it, and the harvest found the id only in Defaults.kys. Identified from the id text, not by execution.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Activate...") is the harvested call, but no menu item uses it; expect nothing to happen (not confirmed by execution).
use_for: nothing in design work; listed so a lookup of this id resolves
avoid: licensing questions: use the Creative Cloud app or Help > Manage My Account...

cards.name: AddArrowHeads2
cards.summary: Most likely the id of the old Add Arrowheads filter (Filter > Stylize > Add Arrowheads... in Illustrator CS3 and earlier), which drew arrowhead and tail shapes as separate objects at the ends of a selected open path. Arrowheads have been a Stroke panel setting since CS5; 30.2.1 has no menu item for this id (a 'Live AddArrowHeads2' effect id is also listed without a menu). Not confirmed by execution.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AddArrowHeads2") is the harvested call but has no menu item; expect nothing (not confirmed). Arrowheads today: Stroke panel (Window > Stroke) or a graphic style applied by script.
use_for: nothing current; for an arrow on an open path use the Stroke panel's Arrowheads
avoid: any arrow job: set Arrowheads and Scale in Window > Stroke instead

cards.name: Adjust Colors Dialog
cards.summary: Probably an older id of the Adjust Colors dialog (Filter > Colors > Adjust Colors... before CS4; today Edit > Edit Colors > Adjust Color Balance..., whose harvested id is 'Adjust3'), which shifts the CMYK, RGB or grayscale values of the selected fills and strokes. No 30.2.1 menu item uses this id; whether it still opens the dialog is unknown.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adjust Colors Dialog") is the harvested call but is unconfirmed; use app.executeMenuCommand("Adjust3") (Adjust Color Balance...) instead, or change item.fillColor / strokeColor values directly (unverified).
use_for: nothing directly; use Edit > Edit Colors > Adjust Color Balance... to warm, cool or darken a whole illustration
avoid: relying on this id in automation; call the current Adjust Color Balance id

cards.name: Adobe AI Device center
cards.summary: Leftover id of the Adobe Device Central link (File > Device Central... in the Creative Suite 3 to 5.5 releases), which previewed artwork on emulated mobile-phone screens. Device Central was discontinued after CS5.5; 30.2.1 has no menu item for it. Identified from the id text, not by execution.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe AI Device center") is the harvested call but no menu item uses it; expect nothing (not confirmed).
use_for: nothing current; preview screen designs by exporting (Asset Export / Export for Screens) and viewing on a real device
avoid: mobile previews: export and check on the device instead

review.changes: summary: Device Central was in Illustrator from CS3, not CS4

cards.name: Adobe Default Workspace
cards.summary: Probably the old command that switched to the default workspace ('[Default]' under Window > Workspace in CS3; the default became 'Essentials' from CS4). In 30.2.1 the default layouts are the workspace presets under Window > Workspace (Essentials, Essentials Classic ...); this id has no menu item and its effect is unconfirmed.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Default Workspace") is the harvested call but unconfirmed; there is no object-model access to workspaces. Choose Window > Workspace > Essentials instead.
use_for: nothing directly; return to the standard layout with Window > Workspace > Essentials, then Reset
avoid: automation that needs a known layout: use the Reset workspace id after picking the workspace by hand

review.changes: removed PS Window/Workspace/Reset Essentials: resetting the current workspace is not switching to the default one

cards.name: Adobe Illustrator About Plug-ins2
cards.summary: Id of an About Plug-ins dialog, which lists the plug-ins Illustrator has loaded with version information. The 30.2.1 Help menu has no About Plug-ins item and the '2' suffix suggests a duplicate or legacy id; whether it still opens anything is unknown. Help > System Info... (id 'systemInfo') may also list the loaded plug-ins (unverified).
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Illustrator About Plug-ins2") is the harvested call but unconfirmed; use app.executeMenuCommand("systemInfo") (Help > System Info...) (may include a plug-in list; unverified).
use_for: checking whether a third-party plug-in loaded (troubleshooting)
avoid: automation: read Help > System Info... instead

review.changes: summary/script_api: System Info listing plug-ins marked unverified

cards.name: Adobe Illustrator Kuler Panel
cards.summary: Leftover id of the Kuler panel (Window > Extensions > Kuler from CS4, later renamed Adobe Color Themes), which browsed, created and synced colour themes from the Kuler / Adobe Color community. The panel is gone from the 30.2.1 Window menu; Adobe Color themes now arrive through Creative Cloud Libraries.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Illustrator Kuler Panel") is the harvested call but no menu item uses it; expect nothing (not confirmed).
use_for: nothing current; build palettes with Window > Color Guide or pull Adobe Color themes from Window > Libraries
avoid: colour themes: use Color Guide, Recolor Artwork or Libraries

review.changes: summary: the Kuler panel arrived in Illustrator CS4, not CS5

cards.name: Adobe Pattern Tile Color
cards.summary: Probably the command id behind Object > Pattern > Tile Edge Color..., which sets the colour of the tile boundary drawn while in Pattern Editing Mode (a display colour only; it does not print or become part of the pattern). The harvest could not pair this id with that item (the keyboard-shortcuts alignment put it at Object > Pattern > Make, an item already paired with another id), so the match is a guess.
cards.how: Pick a colour that contrasts with the pattern art so the tile edge stays visible in Pattern Editing Mode; the walked Tile Edge Color... item is enabled even with no document open, so it can be set before you edit a pattern.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Pattern Tile Color") is the harvested call (unconfirmed); the walked menu item Object/Pattern/Tile Edge Color... has no paired id, so if this works it would only open the colour dialog.
use_for: keeping the tile boundary visible while designing a repeat pattern in a colour close to the default edge colour
avoid: expecting it to change the pattern or its printed colours: it only sets the on-screen tile boundary colour

review.changes: summary: alignment put the id AT Object/Pattern/Make (batch), not next to it; how/avoid: the menu item is enabled with no document, so 'nothing to act on outside Pattern Editing Mode' was wrong

cards.name: Adobe Save a Version
cards.summary: Leftover id of File > Save a Version... from the Version Cue era (Illustrator CS2 to CS4), which saved the open file as a new numbered version with a comment in a Version Cue project. Version Cue was discontinued; in 30.2.1 versions exist only for cloud documents, through File / Window > Version History.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Save a Version") is the harvested call but no menu item uses it; expect nothing (not confirmed). For local versions save numbered copies with doc.saveAs(File(path)) (unverified).
use_for: nothing current; use Version History on cloud documents or numbered Save As copies
avoid: any versioning job: Window > Version History (cloud) or numbered file names

cards.name: AdobeCheatSheetMenu
cards.summary: Purpose not identified: an id listed in Defaults.kys with no menu item in 30.2.1. The name hints at an old quick-reference 'cheat sheet' entry, but that is a guess; treat it as unknown.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AdobeCheatSheetMenu") is the harvested call; its effect is unknown and untested.
use_for: none known
avoid: using it in automation: the effect is unknown

cards.name: AdobeNavigator2
cards.summary: A second, unlisted id that by its name belongs to the Navigator panel (the Window > Navigator menu item uses 'AdobeNavigator'). The Navigator shows a thumbnail of the artwork with a red view box for panning and a zoom slider. Whether this '2' id opens the same panel is not confirmed.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AdobeNavigator2") is the harvested call but unconfirmed; use app.executeMenuCommand("AdobeNavigator") for Window > Navigator.
use_for: nothing beyond Window > Navigator: panning and zooming large posters or multi-artboard files
avoid: automation: call the 'AdobeNavigator' id instead

cards.name: AI Object Mosaic Plug-in3
cards.summary: Probably the command id of Object > Create Object Mosaic..., which turns a selected embedded raster image into a grid of solid-colour vector rectangles, one per tile, coloured from the image. The walked menu item has no paired id and this id is on no menu, so the pairing is inferred from the name only.
cards.how: Select one embedded bitmap; set Tile Spacing, Number of Tiles (or Use Ratio), Result (Color / Gray), resize options and Delete Raster; OK builds a group of rectangles.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AI Object Mosaic Plug-in3") is the harvested call (unconfirmed); if it is Create Object Mosaic it only opens the dialog, since the walked menu item Object/Create Object Mosaic... has no paired id.
use_for: pixel-art or mosaic portrait as editable vector tiles
LED-board or pixel-grid background for a poster
low-res colour grid to recolour with Recolor Artwork
avoid: linked images: embed the image first
large tile counts make thousands of objects and a heavy file; keep the grid coarse

cards.name: AI Toolbox Menu
cards.summary: Probably the old Window > Tools command that showed or hid the toolbox. In 30.2.1 toolbars are under Window > Toolbars (Advanced, Basic, Getting Started, custom toolbars); this id is on no walked menu, so its meaning is inferred from the name only.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AI Toolbox Menu") is the harvested call but unconfirmed; show the toolbar with Window > Toolbars > Advanced instead.
use_for: nothing directly; bring back a hidden toolbar through Window > Toolbars
avoid: automation: the effect is unconfirmed

cards.name: AISlice Feedback Menu
cards.summary: A slice-display id (the harvest's internal-name candidate is 'slice separator'), probably tied to View > Show Slices / Hide Slices, which toggles the drawing of web-slice boundaries and slice numbers on the artboard. Not paired with any 30.2.1 menu item; purpose inferred from the name only.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AISlice Feedback Menu") is the harvested call; its effect is untested. The walked item View/Show Slices has no paired id.
use_for: hiding slice outlines while judging a web graphic's layout
avoid: automation: unconfirmed effect

cards.name: arrangeicon
cards.summary: Leftover Windows id for Window > Arrange Icons, which lined up minimised document windows inside the old multiple-document application window (Illustrator CS3 and earlier; tabbed documents arrived in CS4). Tabbed documents replaced this; 30.2.1 has no such item (the keyboard-shortcuts alignment put it at Window > Workspace > Reset by position only).
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("arrangeicon") is the harvested call but no menu item uses it; expect nothing (not confirmed).
use_for: nothing current; arrange open documents with Window > Arrange (Tile, Cascade, Consolidate All Windows)
avoid: window layout jobs: use Window > Arrange

review.changes: summary: the multiple-document window with Arrange Icons lasted through CS3, not CS2

cards.name: bringAllToFront
cards.summary: The macOS Window > Bring All to Front command, which raises every Illustrator window above other applications' windows. It is a Mac menu item and does not appear on the Windows build that was walked.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("bringAllToFront") is the harvested call; on Windows there is no menu item and it is expected to do nothing (not confirmed). Illustrator's DOM has no app.activate(); on a Mac bring the app forward from outside, e.g. AppleScript: tell application "Adobe Illustrator" to activate (unverified).
use_for: on a Mac: recovering Illustrator documents hidden behind other apps
avoid: Windows: no effect

review.changes: script_api: removed app.activate, which is not an Application member in the AI API harvest

cards.name: Deactivate...
cards.summary: Leftover id from the serial-number licensing era (Help > Deactivate... in Illustrator CS3 to CS6), which released the licence on this computer so it could be activated on another. Creative Cloud versions do this by signing out (Help > Sign Out...); 30.2.1 has no menu item for the id. Identified from the id text, not by execution.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Deactivate...") is the harvested call but no menu item uses it; expect nothing (not confirmed).
use_for: nothing in design work; to free a seat use Help > Sign Out...
avoid: licensing: use Help > Sign Out... or the Creative Cloud app

cards.name: debugPalette
cards.summary: An internal developer 'Debug Palette' (the harvest's internal-name candidate) with the default shortcut Alt+Shift+Ctrl+F12. It is on no menu and undocumented; in a release build it is assumed to do nothing useful, or nothing at all. Not tested.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("debugPalette") is the harvested call; its effect is unknown and untested.
use_for: none in design work
avoid: automation and production files: undocumented internal command
